title: gp prompt-spec
description: Provider-neutral description of one image to produce. The prompting agent writes this and knows nothing about which provider will consume it: the same document is rendered into a Gemini API call, into a Codex Desktop image_gen prompt, or into instructions a human pastes into a web tool. The field vocabulary follows the production-ready prompt structure used by Codex Desktop's image_gen so that rendering to that target is lossless.

id.description: Stable asset id, also the output filename stem. Example: tower_arrow_base.

operation.description: New generation, or an edit of an existing image named in source_image.

source_image.description: Required when operation is 'edit'. Repo-relative path.

edit_goal.description: Required when operation is 'edit'. What must change, and what must stay identical.

style_profile.description: Profile id from profiles/style/, e.g. cel-shaded-outline. Determines which rules the asset gate will apply.

tier.description: A = key art, B = gameplay. Never mix their prompts.

projection.description: Profile id from profiles/projection/. Omit for UI and key art.

facing.description: One of the drawn facings of the projection profile.

part.description: For skeletal assets, which part this is (base, turret, barrel, torso, arm_l...). Parts of one unit MUST share light_direction and palette.

use_case.description: Where this asset is used in the game.

primary_request.description: One sentence: the single thing this image must be.

subject.description: The subject in concrete visual terms — shapes, materials, distinguishing features.

scene.description: Backdrop. For gameplay assets this is normally 'none, transparent background'.

style_medium.description: Rendered from the style profile's prompt_skeleton with this asset's parameters substituted.

composition.description: Framing, orientation, margin, where the pivot/ground contact sits.

lighting.description: Must restate the locked light direction. Parts of one unit that disagree here will not read as one object.

palette.description: Colours this asset may use, drawn from the locked style bible palette.

locked_palette_ref.description: Path to the palette file in the game repo, e.g. art/style/palette.json

emphasis.description: Hex values this asset should lead with.

text.description: Literal text to render, or omit. Generative models render text badly — prefer to composite UI text in engine.

reference_images.description: Repo-relative paths into the frozen art/style/ reference sheet. This is what holds a hundred separately generated assets in one style; a spec for a production asset with an empty list is a bug, not a shortcut.

seed.description: Where the provider supports it. Recorded in provenance either way.
